features.description: Fail-loud gate-state reconciliation. Current gate-state reconciliation can leave the operator debugging stale or contradictory state when persisted gate-state artifacts disagree with declared plan gates. F001 adds an explicit reconciliation helper/error so contradictory persisted state is reported as a platform state problem, not silently normalized. The helper must preserve command_guard-style discipline: deterministic, local, no destructive cleanup, and no mutation before the contradiction is surfaced.
steps: Inspect existing gate-state read/write and reconciliation code in `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/gate_pause.py`, `supervisor.py`, and CLI approve/resume paths.

Define the exact contradictory cases this plan owns: persisted pending/cleared gate not declared by the plan, persisted pending stage incompatible with the current lifecycle stage, and stale active defer state that cannot be mapped to a declared gate.
Add a small typed exception or result object for reconciliation failure with fields for plan_id, gate, stage, persisted_state_path, and remediation.
Wire the helper where gate-state is loaded for dispatch/approve/resume so contradictions fail before any new gate-state write occurs.
Record an INBOX event only after the failure is classified; do not mutate gate-state to auto-repair contradictions.
Add tests with fixture gate-state files covering every owned contradiction and the clean compatibility path from legacy `cleared_gates`-only state.
Run focused gate/resume tests plus the full orchestrate sweep.
features.acceptance: (1) Contradictory gate-state/declaration cases fail loud with a clear typed error, not silent normalization. (2) Error text names the state path, offending gate/stage, and remediation. (3) No gate-state mutation occurs before the error is raised; test asserts file bytes unchanged. (4) Existing legacy `cleared_gates`-only state remains readable and compatible. (5) CLI dispatch/approve/resume paths surface the same reconciliation category consistently. (6) INBOX receives a classified event for operator visibility. (7) Focused gate/resume suite and full orchestrate sweep pass. (8) No schema changes under `claude/shared/`.

evidence_refs.note: 15/15 fixture tests in test_gate_state_reconciliation_f001.py pass: 9 direct unit cases (legacy compat, no-state-file, undeclared in cleared/pause, synthetic prefix allowed, unknown stage, stage-mismatch, stale defer, known defer) + 2 supervisor surfaces (dispatch_volley + dispatch_single_agent) + 4 CLI surfaces (approve refusal, resume --gate refusal, resume --all refusal, clean-state approve). Byte-stability assertions cover acceptance #3.

Full orchestrate sweep with conftest global-config isolation env vars (JARVIS_HOME=/tmp/dp_baseline DONTPANIC_HOME=/tmp/dp_baseline_dp): 1493 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed. Without the env vars, ~50 phantom failures originate from the adjacent conftest gap memo'd as separate scope per D007.

Adds GateStateReconciliationError + reconcile_gate_state + format_reconciliation_inbox_body. Three owned cases enforced: undeclared_gate_name, incompatible_pending_stage, stale_active_defer. Synthetic breaker:/defer:/pre_resume_after_child: prefixes preserved as legitimate.

Adds _reconcile_gate_state_or_raise wrapper invoked at the head of dispatch_single_agent and dispatch_volley, before any gate-state write (pre _arm_parent_pre_resume_gate_for_child / admission reconcile). On failure: INBOX event=gate_state_reconciliation_failed + notify + re-raise.

Adds _reconcile_gate_state_for_cli helper invoked at the head of _approve_main and _resume_main after declared_strs is computed and before approve_gate / resume_all touch state. Returns exit 2 + writes classified INBOX event on contradiction.
New fixture-test module covering all owned contradictions, the legacy compatibility path, supervisor surfaces, and CLI surfaces. Plan IDs follow agent-conventions plan-id pattern.

features.description: Dispatch-time `pre_impl` auto-clear. Ordinary local dev/test dispatches can hit a chicken-and-egg: the operator has already invoked dispatch intentionally, but the first lifecycle gate still forces an immediate `pre_impl` approve/resume cycle before any implementer work can start. F002 adds a conservative auto-clear only for that exact direct-dispatch context. It must write explicit INBOX/gate event evidence so the audit trail remains visible, and it must not weaken protected target or non-dispatch gate discipline.
steps: Identify the canonical dispatch seam after plan load/capability checks and before implementer spawn.
Add a helper that decides whether `pre_impl` may be auto-cleared for this invocation. Inputs must include target_env/target_project, declared gates, invocation context, and current gate-state.
Allow auto-clear only for direct operator dispatch in non-prod/non-protected contexts where `pre_impl` is the only pending lifecycle gate at that stage.
Write the normal gate event plus an INBOX entry naming `auto_cleared_pre_impl`, the command context, and why manual approval was not required.
Preserve explicit manual paths: `dontpanic approve`, `dontpanic resume --gate`, and `dontpanic resume --all` keep their current semantics and do not silently clear unrelated gates.
Add tests covering allowed auto-clear, protected-target refusal, multi-gate refusal, already-cleared idempotency, INBOX evidence, and no implementer spawn before the helper returns.
Run lifecycle gate, CLI resume, and full orchestrate tests.
features.acceptance: (1) Direct dispatch of an eligible dev/test plan with only pending `pre_impl` proceeds without a separate approve/resume command. (2) The gate-state event log records the clearance with an auto-clear reason. (3) INBOX records an operator-readable event naming the auto-clear. (4) Protected/prod plans do not auto-clear. (5) Plans with additional pending gates do not auto-clear beyond the owned `pre_impl` case. (6) Manual approve/resume behavior remains unchanged. (7) Tests prove implementer spawn happens only after the auto-clear decision. (8) Full orchestrate sweep passes.

evidence_refs.note: 11/11 fixture tests in test_pre_impl_auto_clear_f002.py pass: 7 direct unit cases on _maybe_auto_clear_pre_impl (default-False refuses, prod env refuses, PRODUCTION alias refuses, idempotent already-cleared, eligible dev clears + records gate_event/INBOX, multi-gate refusal, pre_impl-not-declared refusal) + 4 dispatch_volley surface cases (direct dispatch proceeds w/o operator action, default direct_dispatch=False pauses, prod target_env override pauses, pre_merge still pauses after pre_impl auto-cleared).
Full orchestrate sweep with conftest global-config isolation env vars: 1504 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed. Net +11 tests over the F001 baseline (1493) — F002 added zero regressions.

Adds _maybe_auto_clear_pre_impl helper with five-clause refusal policy (direct_dispatch + non-prod env + plan declares pre_impl + not already cleared + pre_impl is the only pending pre_impl-stage gate). Wired into dispatch_volley's iteration-0 staged check ahead of the existing pause path. Helper records normal gate_event with actor=supervisor:auto_clear_pre_impl + INBOX event=auto_cleared_pre_impl. dispatch_volley accepts new direct_dispatch kwarg (default False) — programmatic/test invocations preserve the manual contract.

Sets direct_dispatch=True at the two CLI dispatch_volley invocation sites: the legacy `--volley` block (cli main) and the dispatch_from_plan wrapper. CLI approve/resume paths are NOT touched — manual semantics for non-dispatch operator flows remain identical.

New fixture-test module pinning all eight acceptance items including the multi-gate defensive coverage (mocks evaluate_human_gates to return ['pre_impl', 'pre_merge'] for the pre_impl stage even though current staging never produces that shape — guards future staging changes from accidentally widening the carve-out).

features.description: Auditor verdict taxonomy for environmental vs defect findings. Today repeated `needs_changes` can produce `stopped_no_progress` even when the remaining auditor objection is environmental: sandbox cannot run Jest/Xcode, CLI auth cannot reproduce operator evidence, or the auditor is disagreeing with an equivalent evidence shape. F003 adds a conservative classification layer that distinguishes harness/environmental blockers from genuine implementation defects without auto-signing off. It combines an explicit severity taxonomy with operator-facing reporting so no substantive defect is hidden.
steps: Inventory existing audit envelope finding fields and no-progress terminal handling in `supervisor.py` and `circuit_breakers.py`.
Define a closed v0 taxonomy: `implementation_defect`, `environmental_reproduction_failure`, `evidence_shape_disagreement`, `scope_overreach`, and `unknown`.
Implement a pure classifier over structured findings plus known text patterns from the preserved audit trail. Unknown or mixed classifications remain blocking.

Wire classification into the stopped/no-progress terminal path as advisory operator evidence: terminal status remains non-success, but signoff/INBOX/reporting names the classification and recommended next action.
Ensure `implementation_defect` and `unknown` findings remain blocking with no auto-advance.
Add tests using fixtures modeled on the preserved evidence-shape overgating memory, sandbox reproduction failures, and genuine defect examples.
Add an evidence artifact that maps every test fixture to the taxonomy decision and explains why false positives remain bounded.
Run full orchestrate tests and close through the parity objective contract evidence path.
features.acceptance: (1) Classifier is pure and deterministic; no subprocess, network, or filesystem probing. (2) Closed taxonomy values are used consistently in terminal evidence. (3) Environmental/sandbox reproduction failures are classified separately from implementation defects. (4) Evidence-shape disagreement is classified separately from implementation defects only when equivalent saved/operator evidence is present in the audit trail. (5) Mixed or unknown findings remain blocking and are never auto-signed-off. (6) `stopped_no_progress` reporting names the classification and recommended next operator action. (7) Tests cover environmental, evidence-shape, scope-overreach, genuine-defect, mixed, and unknown cases. (8) F2 objective-contract evidence artifacts land under stable filenames.
